title: Retrocompactness of a fixed-rank universal Picard point locus
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be flat, proper and locally of finite presentation, and let $E$ be a finite locally free module on $X$. For $r\in\mathbb N$, the subset of $S$ consisting of points $s$ such that $R(f,E,\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to S)$ [def-sc-picard-universal-rank-match] holds and the tensor pullback of $E$ to $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ is retrocompact: its intersection with every quasi-compact open subset of $S$ is quasi-compact. No representing scheme, connected fibres or surjectivity of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0BDP, first three proof paragraphs: rank decomposition and perfect direct images

proof.text: Use the clopen fibre-rank and empty-fibre loci A and B. A closed subset meets each compact open in a compact set, so each clopen locus is retrocompact and an open retrocompact set is constructible and locally constructible.
Apply ordinary fibre-direct-image rank constructibility to E and to its dual, which is finite locally free by Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.dual. Call the resulting rank-r loci C and D.

The residue criterion proves that the target set is exactly A intersect (B union (C intersect D)). This includes empty fibres of every fixed rank. Finite intersections and unions preserve local constructibility.

On each affine open V, restrict the locally constructible set along the open embedding V into S. Affineness makes the restriction constructible on a compact spectral space. Constructible implies retrocompact, hence compact there, and its image is the intersection with V. Every compact open U is a finite union of affine basis opens by Mathlib eq_finite_iUnion_of_isTopologicalBasis_of_isCompact_open applied to Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens. Distribute intersection over that finite union and apply compactness of a finite union. This proves retrocompactness with no quasi-separatedness hypothesis on S. The private Lean helper proves these steps explicitly.
